extracted.intended_audience: information science educators, ASIS members, and potential nominators for the ASIS Outstanding Information Science Teacher Award
extracted.subtask_short: ASIS Outstanding Information Science Teacher Award
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit criteria for nominating and selecting recipients of the ASIS Outstanding Information Science Teacher Award, describing eligibility, qualities, accomplishments, and the selection/administration process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: direct involvement in teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates for the award must have been directly involved in the teaching of information science, though not necessarily in an academic setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim: 'Candidates for the award must have been d~ectly involved in the teaching of a science information though not necessarily in an academic setting.' This is a fundamental gate criterion for nomination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection by jury and administration
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is administered by the ASIS Education Committee and recipients are selected by a jury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural notes: 'The new award carries an honorarium of $500, donated by ISI, and is administered by the ASIS Education Committee.' The committee/jury evaluates nominees and makes the selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating rules and renominations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations are solicited and candidates may be renominated in future years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim/implication: 'When I wrote my essay ... were the first annual ASIS ... all of them may be renominated ... anyone who wishes a copy of the award criteria can write to: Outstanding Information Science Teacher Award, ASIS.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching excellence and inspirational impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrated excellence in teaching, including the ability to inspire students and make complex topics clear and manageable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the citation: 'He has the great ability to make clear and simple what so often appears complex ... He has inspired many students to research ... Students ... signing up for his courses.' Teaching effectiveness and student engagement are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum development and shaping programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions to developing and shaping information science curricula and creating new courses or programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page cites Lancaster's role: 'instrumental in shaping curriculum ... When he arrived, the school offered just one course ... He has since developed such new courses as ... a course devoted exclusively to bibliometrics.' Curriculum innovation and sustained curricular leadership are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation in course topics and teaching methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction of novel course topics and methods (e.g., bibliometrics, online retrieval, storage systems, measurement and evaluation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete examples: 'course devoted exclusively to bibliometrics', courses on 'storage and online information retrieval', 'measurement and evaluation of library services.' Innovation in subject matter and pedagogical coverage is a selection factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications and textbook authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorship of influential books and monographs that serve as textbooks or foundational texts in information science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence cited: multiple books listed (Vocabulary control; Information retrieval on-line; The measurement and evaluation of library services; etc.) and notes that his 'books have been adopted as textbooks.' Winning book awards (ASIS Best Information Science Book Award, ALA Ralph R. Shaw Award) is highlighted as relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarly output and citation impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarly productivity (articles, chapters, monographs) and measurable citation impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay records 'more than 75 articles, chapters, books ... publications have received 358 citations' in the database cited. Quantity and demonstrable impact of scholarly output are considered supporting evidence of a nominee's contribution to the field and teaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: International reach and influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of international lecturing, guest appearances, and influence in multiple countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lancaster's record is used as exemplar: lectures and guest appearances in Argentina, Brazil, Mexico, Poland, Norway, etc. International recognition and influence beyond the home institution are positive factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition by peers and prior honors
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior awards and honors for scholarship or teaching in related areas are relevant indicators of esteem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page cites prior recognitions (ASIS Best Information Science Book Award, ALA Ralph R. Shaw Award, James Murray Luck Award mentions). Prior external honors bolster a nomination by demonstrating peer recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of practical curriculum/service impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrated use of candidate's work in practical settings (e.g., courses, library services, systems) and influence on professional practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include textbooks adopted for courses, development of practical course offerings (e.g., on bibliometrics or retrieval systems), and influence on library services and evaluation practices. The award values candidates whose teaching has real-world curricular or service impact.
